note: Herdforge lane registry: constraint sections are VERBATIM from chainseer docs/agent/lane-registry.json (the parity contract for the shell->Go swap); lanes[] is the complete forge roster (FAC-127): scout, smith, assayer, orchestrator, scout-planner, verification-gate, review-supervisor, harvest, recovery-sentinel. FAC-142 SurfaceRouter.Decide owns live provider+model+effort+pool for worker and reviewer launches (never harness defaults). Deterministic, no LLM calls. claude-haiku-4-5.reason: claude-haiku silently launches in permission-mode default not auto, so a standing lane prompts the operator on every Bash (measured 2026-07-24 on docs-custodian: its session permissionMode never left default while every sonnet/opus lane held auto). Never route haiku to a standing/autonomous lane; floor a claude standing lane to sonnet.

codex.reason: VERIFIED 2026-07-26: codex exec runs non-interactively (reads the prompt from argv or stdin) and `codex --model M -a never PROMPT` runs an autonomous lane with approvals disabled. codex already drives 6+ standing lanes today. The historical interactive-only rule is retired; codex is a first-class headless surface.

opencode.reason: operator 2026-07-28 supersedes the 2026-07-20 blanket ban: opencode is a FIRST-CLASS harness whatever LLM sits behind it. The 2026-07-20 rule was aimed at the lazer backend, not at opencode, and got recorded on the harness by mistake; `lazer` already carries last_resort under its own entry, and no code ever read this flag, so the ban was prose. What actually made opencode look second-class was two defects, both now fixed: (1) litellm's native `ollama/` adapter emulates tool calls by prompt injection and cannot parse them mid-stream, so a streaming lane emitted tool JSON as prose and harvested no artifacts, fixed in kluster 916815fc by routing all 19 entries through `openai/` + /v1; (2) the herdr state plugin mapped opencode's teardown `session.error` to `blocked`, so a run that finished clean reported a failure to the operator. Route opencode on any backend except lazer, which stays last_resort.

lazer.reason: absolute last resort for every task shape (operator 2026-07-20 / CHA-206). herd-route already enforces this: any healthy or even cap-blocked non-lazer surface wins over lazer. Encoded here so the registry is a complete record of the rule.

agy.reason: the agy Claude pool is shallow and the agy Gemini Pro/Flash pool is deep; default agy work to Gemini. bin/herd-route model_for already selects gemini-* for every agy shape except architecture; the constraint records why.

opencode/deepseek-v4-pro.reason: Direct OpenCode catalog model is reserved for text analysis until an artifact probe proves real tool execution.

opencode/deepseek-v4-flash.reason: Cheap DeepSeek Flash advisory route; never assign to a write-capable pane without a passing artifact probe.

opencode/kimi-k3.reason: Independent Kimi critique route; persistent agent use remains fail-closed pending artifact evidence.

network_capability.note: Whether a provider can reach the network in a given execution MODE. bin/herd-shot runs codex via `codex exec -s read-only|workspace-write`, whose sandbox disables networking by default, so a codex SHOT cannot fetch anything (verified 2026-07-26: a luna/codex research shot ran read-only with no network and honestly refused). The other providers run their real CLI with network. A task shape in shapes_requiring_network must route only to a surface that is network-capable in the current mode. This gates SHOTS: an interactive codex PANE (bin/herd-standing) keeps network and is unaffected, which is why the standing resolver does not filter on this.

codex.reason: codex exec (how herd-shot runs codex) sandboxes the process with networking disabled by default under both -s read-only and -s workspace-write; a shot cannot fetch. codex in an interactive pane keeps network, so this only excludes codex from network-requiring SHOTS.

output_validation.note: A shot's exit code must not lie. A research or schema (structured) shot that returns rc=0 with an empty body, a one-line preamble, or non-JSON where JSON was required has produced garbage; bin/herd-shot validates output non-triviality for these shapes, rejects garbage (rc nonzero), and reroutes ONCE to the next eligible provider before failing. Evidence 2026-07-26: a grok research shot returned rc=0 with a one-line preamble and no report.

standard.reason: quota-aware waterfall on the declared route_shape; no provider pin and no model floor. A soft `prefer` (if the lane declares one) is tried first and falls back to the waterfall. cost_tier is an ENFORCED CEILING (CHA-894), not a description of the pick: a lane whose waterfall choice exceeds it is demoted to the best in-tier model for its provider, and where a model_pin or a model_floor_class forbids that, it escalates with an explicit cost_ceiling reason recorded in the resolved payload. Silent escalation is impossible.
